title: A sales report with LINQ
description:
Answer business questions about customers, products and orders using LINQ joins and grouping.

```
Revenue by city: London 1,240.00, Paris 610.00
Top product: Keyboard (14 sold)
Customers with no orders: Dee, Eve
Monthly totals: Jan 520.00, Feb 830.00, Mar 500.00
```
hints: Join orders to products first to get each line's value, then group by whatever the question asks (lesson 8.01).
`(1240m).ToString("N2", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)` formats money the same on every computer.
requirements: Three lists of records: customers, products and orders (with a product id, a quantity and a date).
Each answer is one LINQ query; at least one uses `Join`, one `GroupJoin` and one `GroupBy`.
Print money with `:N2` and the invariant culture.
stretch: Rewrite one query in query syntax with `join ... into` and compare.
